response.question: I ordered an iPhone from an online shopping website for ₹65,000, but the package contained a cheap dummy phone. I've contacted customer support several times, but they keep rejecting my refund request. What are my consumer rights?
response.answer:
If you bought the phone for personal use, you are generally a consumer even though you ordered it online. Receiving a dummy instead of the advertised iPhone may support a complaint about defective goods or an unfair trade practice. The facts would need to be examined.

Refusing to take back defective goods and refund the price can itself be an unfair trade practice if the conditions in the Act are met. The relevant period is the one stated on the bill or receipt, or 30 days if none is stated. Whether this applies to your request depends on the facts.

You can make a consumer complaint seeking a refund or replacement. If the complaint is proved, a District Consumer Commission can order a refund, replacement, or compensation for loss or injury due to the other party’s negligence. The Commission decides the outcome; a refund is not guaranteed.

The current financial limits for deciding which Consumer Commission can hear your complaint must be checked. They are set by Rules not available in these sources.

response.question: I purchased a weight-loss product after seeing an advertisement claiming that it would show results in 15 days. It didn't work at all, and now the company is refusing to refund me. Can I take action against the company for misleading advertising?
response.answer:
Yes. You may have grounds to complain about the advertisement. A claim that a product has benefits it does not have can be an unfair trade practice. Whether the 15-day claim was misleading depends on the evidence; the fact that it did not work for you does not by itself settle that question. [consumer_protection_act_2019:2]

You can consider a consumer complaint seeking a refund. If a District Consumer Commission finds that a defect or unfair trade practice is proved, it can order the price to be returned. A refund is not guaranteed. [consumer_protection_act_2019:2; consumer_protection_act_2019:39]

For an advertisement affecting consumers generally, you can also send a complaint in writing or electronically to the District Collector, the regional office Commissioner, or the Central Consumer Protection Authority. After investigation, the Central Authority may direct that a misleading advertisement be stopped or changed. [consumer_protection_act_2019:17; consumer_protection_act_2019:21]

response.question: I bought a second-hand car from a dealer in Delhi. He assured me that the car was in perfect condition, but within a week the engine developed a serious problem. The dealer says he is not responsible because I bought a used car. Do I have any legal protection?
response.answer:
Yes, you may have legal protection. The fact that the car is second-hand does not, by itself, settle whether the dealer is responsible.

The dealer’s assurance that the car was in perfect condition matters. A defect can include a failure to meet the quality claimed by the trader. A false statement about quality, including an oral statement, can also be an unfair trade practice. Whether the engine problem shows that the assurance was false will depend on the evidence. [consumer_protection_act_2019:2]

If you bought the car by description from a dealer who sells cars of that description, there can also be an implied condition that it is of merchantable quality—that is, of a saleable quality appropriate to what was sold. If you examined the car, this condition does not cover defects that your examination ought to have revealed. The car’s used condition and the sale terms may be relevant. [sale_of_goods_act_1930:16]

If you bought the car for personal use, you will generally qualify as a consumer. Purchases for resale or a commercial purpose are generally excluded, with an exception for goods used exclusively to earn a livelihood through self-employment. A consumer complaint can allege defective goods or an unfair trade practice. [consumer_protection_act_2019:2]

If a complaint is proved, a Consumer Commission may order remedies such as removal of the defect or return of the price; the decision depends on the case. A claim for damages for breach of warranty may also be possible. Neither outcome is guaranteed. [consumer_protection_act_2019:39; sale_of_goods_act_1930:59]

The available Sale of Goods Act text is consolidated, but its exact consolidation date is unknown. A lawyer can check the current text when assessing your case.

response.question: How much time do I have to file a consumer complaint after the problem happened?
response.answer:
A consumer complaint must generally be filed within two years from the date the cause of action arose—that is, when the events giving rise to the complaint occurred. The relevant date depends on the facts of your case.

If more than two years have passed, the Consumer Commission may still consider the complaint if you satisfy it that you had a sufficient reason for the delay. The Commission must record its reasons for accepting the delay.

response.question: The company I want to complain against is in another city. Can I file my consumer complaint where I live?
response.answer:
Yes, potentially. If your complaint belongs before a District Commission, you can file it in the district where you live. The company being in another city does not by itself prevent this. The State Commission also allows filing where the complainant lives. [consumer_protection_act_2019:34; consumer_protection_act_2019:47]

Which Commission can hear your complaint depends on its jurisdiction. The current money limits are set by rules that are not available in these sources, so please check them before filing. [consumer_protection_act_2019:34]

response.question: My new pressure cooker exploded because of a manufacturing defect and I was injured. Can I claim compensation from the manufacturer?
response.answer:
I’m sorry you were injured. Yes, you can bring a product liability claim against the manufacturer for harm caused by a defective cooker. This is a claim for compensation for harm caused by a product. Personal injury counts as harm.

A manufacturer can be liable if the product has a manufacturing defect. If a product liability claim is proved, the District Consumer Commission can award compensation. The outcome and amount are not guaranteed; the Commission decides based on the case.

response.question: The shop bill says 'goods once sold will not be taken back'. Can the shop refuse to take back a defective product because of this?
response.answer:
Not necessarily. A “no returns” statement on the bill does not by itself prevent you from complaining about a defective product. Refusing to take back defective goods and refund the price can be an unfair trade practice, subject to the period stated on the bill or receipt. If no period is stated, the Act refers to 30 days. Whether the wording on your bill affects that period may be disputed. [consumer_protection_act_2019:2]

A consumer complaint can be made about defective goods. If the relevant complaint is proved, a Consumer Commission may order a remedy such as repair, replacement or a refund. The outcome depends on the facts and the Commission’s decision. [consumer_protection_act_2019:2; consumer_protection_act_2019:39]

response.question: Online order kiya tha, paise kat gaye lekin delivery nahi hui aur seller refund nahi de raha. Main kya kar sakta hoon?
response.answer:
Aap consumer complaint karne par vichar kar sakte hain. Online kharidari bhi consumer law ke daayre mein aa sakti hai [consumer_protection_act_2019:2]. Jo samaan bechne ya deliver karne ka agreement hua tha, uske baare mein consumer complaint di ja sakti hai [consumer_protection_act_2019:35].

Aap complaint mein refund maang sakte hain. Agar service ki kami jaise aarop saabit hote hain, to Consumer Commission paise wapas karne ka order de sakta hai. Faisla Commission karega; refund pakka nahi hai [consumer_protection_act_2019:39].

Ek doosra raasta bhi hai: agar seller galat tareeke se samaan deliver karne se inkaar karta hai ya delivery mein laparwahi karta hai, to buyer nuksan ke liye seller par case kar sakta hai [sale_of_goods_act_1930:57]. Is source ke consolidated text ki exact date available nahi hai.
